verdict: P108-NEGATIVES-EXPANSION (grow the gate specificity bound using every committed real known-planet host, offline): p103 skipped 3 single-sector hosts; their curves are committed and their systems are catalogued, so they are legitimate labelled negatives. Measured the same way as p103 and fed to the frozen gate, all 3 land tier none -> the labelled-negative union grows 12 -> 15 (15/15 refused, 0 false promotion(s), specificity 1.000), tightening the Wilson 95% lower bound on the true-negative rate 0.757 -> 0.796. Honest ceiling: reaching the protocol's 0.95 precision bar on a zero-false-claim bound needs >= 73 clean real negatives -- we have 15; the gap is sample size of real labelled planets, not method. On 2/3 single-sector hosts the strongest BLS peak did NOT match the catalogued planet -- a lone sector mis-detects even a known signal, the direct case for requiring cross-sector corroboration. Sensitivity arm (promoting a clean novelty) remains synthetic-only (p100). No claim, no gate.
